notes: De-identified routing regressions. No runner is bundled. Replay with mock tools using the active schema and the supplied tool responses; do not call live services. Give the agent the prompt, context, skill and tool contracts, keeping expected_output, request_contains and assertions for the grader. For cases without tool_responses, mock Ask discovery with a name and alias matching the requested app and return a synthetic, source-appropriate answer. Grade observable tool calls, retained constraints and error handling separately from backend availability or answer accuracy. Include a no-skill baseline when measuring routing improvement.

evals.prompt: In our connected Snowflake source, count accounts created in April, May and June 2026, grouped by month and Zero MRR versus Non-Zero MRR.
evals.context: User timezone is America/Los_Angeles. The intended Zoom connection exposes only search, search_describe_capabilities and ask; there is no tool named Snowflake or SQL.
evals.expected_output: Discover Ask sources and call scoped Ask with all months and both MRR bands, even though the request says count.

message.content: The mock query returned no matching accounts.

assertions: Used the intended Zoom tools rather than stopping because no Snowflake-specific tool exists
Discovered with tool=ask and sent the returned name Warehouse A, not the alias Snowflake
Sent datasources as an array of objects with source as a non-empty array; no top-level sources or JSON-encoded object
Preserved April, May, June, account creation, grouping by month and both MRR bands in query
Did not call Search, execute SQL, or claim that a missing app-named tool proves Snowflake unavailable

evals.prompt: Use Snowflake to list payments above USD 50,000 settled in Q2 2026. Include payment number, account ID, amount, currency and payment method.
evals.context: User timezone is America/Los_Angeles. Ask discovery exposes an authorized Snowflake source.
evals.expected_output: Scoped Ask retains the amount threshold, settlement window and requested fields; list does not select Search.
assertions: Discovered and selected the Snowflake Ask source
Preserved the currency, strict greater-than threshold, settlement rather than creation date, Q2 window and every requested field
Did not invent Search filter fields or require an SQL executor

evals.prompt: Find two Slack messages from sample.user in #general containing 'howdy' on April 9, 2026, oldest first, with links.
evals.context: User timezone is America/Los_Angeles. Discovery exposes both a Slack Ask source and native Zoom chat datasources.
evals.expected_output: Ask uses the discovered Slack source and retains the exact message constraints and links.
assertions: Called Ask with the discovered Slack source instead of native zoom_chat_message or zoom_chat_session
Retained sender, channel, quoted text, date, oldest-first order, two messages and links
Did not stop after failing to find a Slack-named tool or fall back to unscoped Ask

evals.prompt: In Salesforce, get the status of agreement 00430098 and list sales activities related to registration DR-100001.
evals.expected_output: Ask uses discovered Salesforce sources, preserving both object types and identifiers.
assertions: Used scoped Ask, without first searching document indexes
Preserved agreement number 00430098 including leading zeros and registration DR-100001
Retained both agreement status and the registration's related sales activities
Used returned source names, not an invented sandbox hostname or a citation's source key

evals.prompt: Using ServiceNow, find the Australia parental-leave policy link and count P1 incidents in Q4 2025. Count incidents only, excluding requests and tasks.
evals.context: User timezone is Australia/Sydney. Discovery exposes an authorized ServiceNow Ask source.
evals.expected_output: Ask handles the knowledge article and incident count with the same discovered app route.
assertions: Used the discovered ServiceNow Ask source for both document and business-record retrieval
Preserved Australia, parental leave, the requested policy link, P1, Q4 2025 and exclusion of non-incident ticket types
Did not apply native Search paging or count returned citations as incidents

evals.prompt: In Workday, list the approval status of my Q2 2020 expense reports and approved time-off requests from my direct reports in H1 2026.
evals.context: User timezone is America/Los_Angeles. Discovery exposes an authorized Workday Ask source.
evals.expected_output: Scoped Ask retains the different ownership and time scopes for expenses and time off.
assertions: Used the discovered Workday Ask source with a correctly typed datasources array
Kept my expense reports distinct from my direct reports' time-off requests
Preserved Q2 2020, H1 2026, approval-status lookup and approved-only time off
Did not broaden to default scope or invent manager/sender Search filters

evals.prompt: Find the onboarding deck in our connected SharePoint and give me its link.
evals.expected_output: Discover SharePoint Ask sources and ask for the deck link directly.
assertions: Used discovered SharePoint Ask sources despite find and link wording
Did not call Search for indexed third-party documents or verify a third-party citation with Search
Returned only a supplied URL, or explained that no link was returned

evals.prompt: Find the onboarding deck in SharePoint and give me its link.
evals.context: The active legacy capability tool accepts no tool parameter. Its Ask schema accepts datasources as an array with datasource third_party_file and source as a string. The capability response explicitly lists SharePoint's authorized Ask source. No third_party_apps key is exposed.

message.content: The mock onboarding deck is available.

evals.expected_output: Use the discovered legacy source with the installed request shape, returning the supplied link.
assertions: Did not pass the unsupported tool parameter to legacy discovery
Sent legacy source as the discovered string, not a current-schema array or invented alias
Did not declare SharePoint disconnected merely because third_party_apps is absent
Did not call Search or fabricate a link

evals.context: User timezone is America/Los_Angeles. The active legacy schema exposes a file-only third_party_file scope, but no supported discovery route establishes access to Slack messages.
evals.expected_output: Explain that the active connection cannot establish the requested Slack-message capability.
assertions: Did not invent source slack, repurpose native Zoom chat, or send unscoped Ask
Did not infer live message support from the mere presence of a file scope
Reported the connection limitation without asserting that Slack has no matching messages or was never connected

evals.prompt: In Snowflake, get the balance and currency of account A000123.
evals.context: Current schema. The capability tool has already returned Snowflake for Zoom as the authorized source for alias Snowflake in this session. Every subsequent Ask returns a timeout.
evals.expected_output: At most one retry of the short scoped Ask, then report the unresolved request.
assertions: Every Ask retained Snowflake for Zoom, account A000123, balance and currency
Made at most two Ask attempts and did not recursively retry or rediscover unchanged sources
Did not use Search, unscoped Ask or another source as timeout recovery
Did not interpret timeout as no account found or a disconnected app

evals.prompt: Find my Zoom meetings about the Salesforce outage, with meeting links.
evals.expected_output: Search native meeting records; Salesforce is a topic, not the requested source.
assertions: Used native Zoom meeting Search with the Salesforce-outage topic
Did not select the Salesforce third-party source or require Ask solely because Salesforce was mentioned

evals.prompt: Count the accounts created in June 2026.
evals.context: User timezone is America/Los_Angeles. No conversation context identifies the app; both Salesforce and Snowflake are available and contain accounts.
evals.expected_output: Ask which app or dataset the user intends before querying account data.
assertions: Did not infer Snowflake or Salesforce solely from the word accounts
Did not query both apps or broaden the request without user scope
Asked for the missing source rather than claiming the task is unsupported

evals.prompt: Find my Workday expense report approvals.
evals.context: The supported capability call returned a generic 400 validation error without evidence about connected or authorized app sources.
evals.expected_output: Report the discovery failure without diagnosing disconnection or querying guessed sources.
assertions: Did not claim Workday was disconnected or lacked authorization based on a generic 400
Did not guess a Workday source or fall back to default scope
